requiredFindings.location: PLAN.md:42 and PLAN.md:183 (§1 performance bullet and §5.1)
requiredFindings.claim: Each product benchmark takes the median of 7 runs after 3 warmups, and a regression fails above ×1.20 time or ×1.25 RSS.
requiredFindings.fix: State the two statistics separately. AQ §3 records 3 warmups and 7 measured runs, then the gate takes the median elapsed time and the maximum of the seven per-run peak RSS samples. The limits are 1.20× median time and 1.25× baseline peak RSS, plus the fixture's reviewed absolute bounds. Do not describe RSS as a median.

requiredFindings.claim: A missing semantic rung is typed and indeterminate, never a weaker answer, and that single outcome is D-007 item 8 and DR-G25.
requiredFindings.fix: Split the two decided rules. D-007 item 8 requires a typed, loud refusal rather than degrading to a weaker parser, syntactic tier, semantic model, graph, or finding model. DR-G25's acceptance text is Coverage-indeterminate for a missing required TypeScript semantic rung, with no silent syntax fallback; its product expansion is no silent fallback for input-closure, resolution, external-world, and coverage deficiencies, and it does not say every missing rung is indeterminate. The M3 routing at BP:1029 can stay.

requiredFindings.claim: Findings carry messageCode and parameters only, cited to IE:1282-1286.
requiredFindings.fix: Cite the finding shape, not the parameter-digest record. finding3 carries a nullable fingerprint and correspondence state, rule closure and ruleId, subject3 and display attribution, message code and parameters, severity, and evidence references. FindingSurface requires findingId, ruleId, subjectId, subjectPath, severity, messageCode, correspondence, fingerprint, and waived. IE:1282-1286 is only the parameter digest {messageCode, parameters}. Keep the real gap: there is no explanation-quality requirement and no per-finding remedy or suggested action. Remedies on terminations can stay.

requiredFindings.claim: The proposed analyze budgets are measured on the slowest D-102 runner class each size class is held to, and M6 runs G13 qualification on D-102 runners.
requiredFindings.fix: Remove D-102 as the analyze and G13 runner. D-102 adopts the hosted fleet class for G03/G04 and states that it does not name G13. D-006 binds its runner classes to DR-G01–G05 and puts analyze RSS deliberately outside those thresholds. Name the runner the plan actually wants, and ask for it as its own decision if it is not the existing G13 profile.

requiredFindings.claim: An exploratory quality report uses the product-quality report schema with standing "exploratory", consistent with AQ:212-214, and no schema successor is asked for.
requiredFindings.fix: The schema is closed (additionalProperties false) and has no standing member. AQ:212-214 says synthetic reports are tagged reference-only and cannot be promoted; it does not add a standing field or a class for real pre-qualification measurements. Add a §11 decision for a report-schema successor that names the non-qualifying class, and stop saying schema v3 already accepts standing.

requiredFindings.claim: The harness fetches each T2 repository at the pinned commit, and no source is vendored. That fetch is not flagged against the offline qualification rule.
requiredFindings.fix: Separate corpus acquisition from the qualified run. Ordinary analysis is offline, with no implicit download (AQ:346). DR-G06 requires supported runs with no network, and the preview G13 workload is no-network. State that pinned bytes and the tree digest are inputs to the harness, and that the qualified run does not fetch. If acquisition itself needs a recorded exception, name that decision in §11.

requiredFindings.claim: Knip, ts-prune, rustc dead_code/unused, and cargo-udeps/cargo-machete supply recall misses inside claimed-complete scope, this is consistent with D-007 and BP:716-717, and M6 scores that recall inside G13. No gate successor is asked for.
requiredFindings.fix: BP:716-717 forbids a PATH or system compiler as an implicit provider fallback. D-007 item 8 forbids degrading to a weaker model. Neither text admits those tools as qualification oracles. QG items[12] evidence is per-cell exact observations, Coverage negatives, and the performance profile, not a cross-tool differential. Either keep the differentials outside G13 and say so, or add a §11 decision that amends DR-G13 and states that the oracle tools are pinned harness inputs and never the product analyzer.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The 11×6 cell count and the 57/6/3 split are true of native-capability-matrix.v2.json: 11 capabilities including inventory, 57 SUPPORTED-DESIGN, 6 UNSUPPORTED-TYPED, 3 NOT-SELECTED. NE:584-616 does not state those numerals. Its table omits inventory, so the visible rows are 60 cells, and L-CL1 is line 617, one line past the citation. Point the count at the matrix and extend the limitation citation through 617.

There is no churn metric and no record that declares a rename or move as the same finding-key2. Correspondence itself is specified: finding3 has matched|unmatched state (common.schema.json Correspondence and UnmatchedOccurrence reasons), IE:211-212 requires explicit subject correspondence for a rename, and WS:383-389 does not mint a fingerprint for an unmatched occurrence or classify it as CODE-NET-NEW by default. O6 should say the declaration mechanism is absent, not that correspondence is absent. IE:1564-1567 supports the unmatched state; the rename requirement is IE:211-212.

There is no analyze latency or RSS budget for JS, Rust, or syntax-only cells, and DR-G05 caps remain deferred by D-006 with no number. A worst-case graph bound does exist for graph queries: page size at most 1,000, produced items at most 100,000, semantic depth at most 64, visited nodes at most 1,000,000 (workflows-and-surfaces.md:1163-1165). O3 should limit the absent bound to analyze, not to every graph operation.

O9 is right that QG items[12] still says cold/warm p95 and thresholds DECIDED by D-369, while AQ §3 is the median/maximum regime. The same preview regime is still written as acceptance method in analysis-quality-completion.v2.md:136-150 (5 warmups, 30 samples, nearest-rank p95, 10% regression) and that file's §4 still emits PASS/FAIL/NON-PASS. D1 names only the QG text. The hygiene list's four corpus denials are real (02-distribution-and-components.md:336-338, prototype-evidence-reference.md:26-30, 05-v1-to-v2-relationship.md:102, register DR-203 at 08-decision-and-readiness-register.md:329). A fifth denial is 11-three-reviewer-direction-synthesis.md:290, which the plan quotes as current motivation; that synthesis also says it is steering advice and not a register amendment (lines 297-299). Chapter 02:339-341 still says V2 invents no support list, against 10-mvp-and-future-scope.md:41.

Recording manual-correction counts is required (FW-14 in current-source-map.proposed.md:67; CH13:77-84). CH13:82-83 says no numeric target is invented there. Q8's measurement exists; the target of 0 for conventional shapes is this plan's proposal, not an already decided gate like Q1.

The accepted product rule surface is PolicyDocumentV2 (workflows-and-surfaces.md:592-610). The DSL citation WS:621-649 is the waiver and policy-test text; the strong-Kleene rule is WS:600-604. CH13:37-40 keeps the preview to one bundled import-cycle rule and does not enable an additional rule pack. D2 should treat a first-party pack as a successor against that boundary. The gap O2 is real: dead-code rules appear as workflow fixture ids such as no-unused-export and rs-no-dead-fn, and the preview ships module-import-cycle only (analysis-quality-completion.v2.md:53-63).
